subsection: 3. Careers in food and related industries

notes.h: Careers in food production and manufacturing
points: Production operative: runs and monitors processing and packaging machinery on a food production line.
Food technologist: develops new products and processes, and improves recipes and methods for shelf life and quality.
Quality control technician: tests raw materials and finished products against specifications and food safety standards.
Food microbiologist: tests food and production surfaces for microbes that cause spoilage or food poisoning.
Butcher, baker and confectioner: traditional craft trades in retail shops or food manufacturing.
Food engineer: designs, runs and maintains processing and packaging plant so that it operates safely and efficiently.

notes.h: Careers in food service and hospitality
points: Chef: plans menus, prepares, cooks and presents food in restaurants, hotels and institutions.
Caterer: plans and delivers food for events, canteens and institutions such as hospitals and schools.
Waiter or waitress: serves food and drink and takes orders in restaurants, hotels and bars.
Hotel or restaurant manager: controls costs, stock and staffing for a food and accommodation business.

notes.h: Careers in health, nutrition and education
points: Dietitian: assesses nutritional needs and plans diets for individuals and groups, including people with illness or special needs.
Nutritionist: advises on healthy eating, often in public health, sport or the food industry.
Home Economics teacher: teaches food, nutrition and family and consumer studies in second-level schools.
Environmental Health Officer: inspects food premises and enforces food hygiene law; in Ireland EHOs work for the HSE Environmental Health Service.

notes.h: Careers in agri-food, science and marketing
points: Agricultural scientist: researches crop and livestock production, food quality and farm efficiency.
Marketing and sales staff: promote products to retailers and consumers and develop export sales.
Buyer: sources ingredients and packaging from suppliers at the required quality and price.
Food safety scientist: tests and assesses food safety risks for regulators, producers and retailers.

notes.h: Employers and routes into food careers
points: State bodies such as Bord Bia, Teagasc, Bord Iascaigh Mhara (BIM), the Food Safety Authority of Ireland (FSAI) and the HSE employ scientists, advisers, inspectors and marketing staff.
Local authorities employ Environmental Health Officers to inspect food premises.
Food manufacturers and retailers employ production, quality, technical and sales staff.
Entry routes include apprenticeships, further education and training courses, and third-level degrees in food science, dietetics or culinary arts.

keyTerms.definition: A professional who develops new food products and processes and improves existing ones for quality and shelf life.
The testing of raw materials and finished products against set standards to keep their quality and safety consistent.
A scientist who tests food for microbes that cause spoilage or illness.
A qualified health professional who assesses nutritional needs and plans diets for individuals and groups.
A professional who advises on healthy eating and nutrition, often in public health, sport or the food industry.
An HSE officer who inspects food premises and enforces food hygiene law.
A person or business that plans and provides food for events, canteens and institutions.

factCards.term: Three science-based careers in the food industry
factCards.definition: Food technologist, who develops products; quality control technician, who tests quality; food microbiologist, who tests for microbes.

factCards.term: Three duties of an Environmental Health Officer in food premises
factCards.definition: Inspecting food premises; enforcing food hygiene law; taking samples for testing.
Assessing nutritional needs; planning diets for illness or special needs.
Chef; caterer; waiter or waitress; hotel or restaurant manager.

factCards.term: Three routes into a food career
factCards.definition: Apprenticeship; further education and training course; third-level degree in food science, dietetics or culinary arts.

factCards.term: Three state bodies that employ food scientists or inspectors
factCards.definition: Teagasc, Bord Iascaigh Mhara (BIM) and the Food Safety Authority of Ireland (FSAI).

questions.prompt: Outline the main duties of two careers in the food industry, one in food production and one in food service.
questions.model: Food production, any one with duties: food technologist develops new products and processes and tests shelf life and recipes; quality control technician samples raw materials and finished goods against specifications; food microbiologist tests food for microbes. Food service, any one with duties: chef plans menus, prepares and cooks food and controls portions and costs; caterer plans and delivers food for events and institutions. One mark for each career and one for each duty stated, up to the marks available.

questions.prompt: Discuss the range of careers available in the food industry, referring to production, food service, health and science. Outline the routes and qualifications needed to enter them.
questions.model: Production: production operatives, food technologists, quality control technicians, food microbiologists, food engineers and craft trades such as butcher, baker and confectioner. Food service: chefs, caterers, waiters and waitresses, hotel and restaurant managers. Health and science: dietitians and nutritionists advising on diet, Environmental Health Officers inspecting food premises for the HSE, agricultural scientists and food safety scientists. Employers: state bodies such as Bord Bia, Teagasc, BIM, FSAI and the HSE; food manufacturers and retailers. Routes: apprenticeships, further education and training courses, and third-level degrees in food science, dietetics or culinary arts.
